question.text: 'Aravalli Growth Fund III', a Category II AIF, is nearing its Final Close. What is the maximum number of investors permitted in the scheme under SEBI (AIF) Regulations (ignoring Accredited Investor exclusion for now)?

answer.text: 1,000 investors per scheme (accredited investors excluded from the count under the 2025 amendment)
49 investors per scheme, consistent with Companies Act private placement limits

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 10(f): no scheme of an AIF shall have more than 1,000 investors. Per SEBI (AIF) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025 (w.e.f. Nov 19, 2025), Accredited Investors are excluded from this count. Angel Funds have a lower cap of 200. For AIFs structured as a Company, the Companies Act private-placement cap of 200 applies separately. **The Trap:** Option A is the Angel-Fund / Companies-Act cap. Option D is the old Companies Act private-placement ceiling of 49 (now 200). Option C is wrong — a ceiling does exist. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A and XIX-B both test the 1,000 cap. XIX-C adds the recent AI-exclusion amendment and Angel-Fund carve-out. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: Track AI-onboarding carefully in the Investor Register — post-2025 amendment, an AI-heavy Cat I/II can scale beyond 1,000 counting only non-AI investors. But if a previously-AI investor loses status, the fund must monitor whether the non-AI count has now breached 1,000. This belongs in the Compliance Test Report.
